preview: An internship interview experience at Citi detailing the online assessment, technical round, and HR round with helpful preparation tips.
content:
INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Nishith Savla 
TY CE 
 
CRITERIA 
1. CGPA of 6.5 and above 
2. No active backlog 
 
Note: The complete process was online.
1 
 
Pre-Placement Talk 
Duration: 1 hr 
This is the time where you understand about the company, its goals, its objectives and their 
work areas. It is a great time for you to ask any questions you have about the role, the process 
and anything you have in mind related to the upcoming internship process. It might seem like a 
waste of time to a few but it’s not. You can use the company’s language and values in your 
answers which could give you an upper hand in the interview process. 
 
Online Assessment 
Duration: 1 hr 
 
The sections were different for each role. As I had set the 1st preference as ICG (Institutional 
Clients Group) division, I had the following format: 
1. Coding Questions (30 mins):  
1. Count perfect squares in a list (Array). 
2. Create a list of first negative number in each sub-list of size k (Sliding window). 
 
2. SQL MCQs (12 questions in 15 minutes) 
 
3. React MCQs (12 questions in 15 minutes) 
 
4. Angular MCQs (12 questions in 15 minutes) 
 
Switching between the sections was not allowed. For the MCQ sections, you couldn’t switch 
between questions, nor visit a previously answered question. The test had camera and 
microphone proctoring. 
 
I finished the coding section in around 30 mins. It was funny that when I ran the code once it 
showed 12 / 13 test cases passed but when the same code was ran again, it gave 13 / 13 
passed.
2 
 
While filling up the form for Citi, we were presented with 2 roles: ICG Tech and EIO&T and we 
had to specify our preference for these 2 roles, where I filled it in the order ICG then EIO&T.  
 
When the list of shortlisted candidates came, 20 people were shortlisted for ICG Tech; 20 
people were shortlisted and 10 were waitlisted for PBWM Tech (this role wasn’t specified 
earlier but somehow came up in the shortlist). The list for EIO&T came the next night where 8 
students had been shortlisted. 
 
Technical Round 
Duration: 1 hr (mine was at 12 pm) 
 
The interview started with my introduction. Since I mentioned that I was the Cloud Computing 
Lead at GDSC, he asked me about my role and contribution in that. I briefly described my 
further plans being the Cloud Computing Lead since our tenure had started very recently. Then 
he went ahead and asked me about my projects on my Résumé, I explained all of them. One of 
my projects was a password manager which used AES-256 encryption and SHA-256 hashing 
algorithm and he asked me how I implemented that. I told him that I used a library provided by 
dart for the encryption and walked him through the encryption flow. I assumed this was to 
check if I really knew how the project works. 
Next, he asked me which language I am comfortable in for the interview to which I answered 
Python and JavaScript. He asked me a few basic python questions like are parameters passed by 
value or by reference and a few other questions assessing my knowledge in the field of Python. 
He also asked me if I had created any projects in Python. I explained him an Alert Automation 
project I had done for a freelance client. He couldn’t get the idea for the first time but 
eventually I did explain it to him. I also told him about a Generative AI project I was working on 
in Python using GPT-3.5 and he did find it interesting. 
After that, he asked me if I knew SQL and asked me a query to delete duplicate names from a 
table. I answered with a nested query which I could of think of that time with an explanation. 
There was a 1-minute silence after that, he was probably typing the query for the review and 
then asked me again if I could come up with something better. I sincerely told him that I wasn’t 
completely confident about its correct. I couldn’t think of any other better solution. He liked my 
approach and since I was almost near to the answer, he was satisfied with it. 
Finally, he asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him a day in life of Summer Analyst 
Intern, and he briefed me about that.
3 
 
HR Round 
Duration: 20 minutes 
After a long wait (ghost) of 5 hours, we were finally shortlisted for the HR Round. The 
interviewer was very friendly and asked me to introduce myself and asked me which topics had 
been already covered in previous round so that the same questions are not repeated. He also 
introduced himself and briefed about not just his work life but his off-work life too. 
Walking through my Résumé, he asked me about my Diploma and why I did I choose to do that 
instead of HSC. I explained my ideology behind the decision. Later, he asked me how I got into 
Computers. I told him that we had an old computer since my childhood but didn’t get a chance 
to use it much and how slowly that longing and curiosity got me into computers. He could 
relate with me since he had a similar childhood. It seemed like a good friendly conversation 
than an interview. He also asked me if my experience assembling my first computer since he 
had done that in childhood. But I had never assembled any PC and told him the truth about the 
same. 
Then he asked me in this highly competitive world how will you stand out? My answer to this 
question was that I attend a lot of meetups and events to stay up-to-date and build 
connections, I have also learnt various technologies including Linux and Git (which is a very 
important tool when working with a team and anyway, it’s not about competing it’s 
collaborating and learning from each other’s strengths and weaknesses. It was not the best 
answer I could think of, but it seems to have done the job. 
At the end, when he asked me if I had any questions for him, I asked him how a day would look 
like in his life or in the life of an Intern (I poorly framed it). He was kind enough to give a brief 
info about both. 
 
Result 
We received the shortlist later that evening and 10 students were selected (5 for PBWM and 5 
for ICG). The process for EIO&T was held the next day where 2 out of 8 students got selected.
4 
 
TIPS 
1. Follow any DSA sheet you want. Striver, Arsh Goyal, Love Babbar all have their own 
curated sets of problems. Since I chose to do DSA in Python, I liked the Neetcode 75 
better since whenever I used to get stuck, Neetcode would have a solution made 
especially in Python. It doesn’t matter where you practice from, all that matters is your 
understanding of the concept.  
Also, some folks (even seniors) would recommend not to use Python and the reasons 
are completely baseless. Yes, you do may more TLE errors than other languages but all it 
does is it forces you to write more optimal code with better time complexity. And using 
Python, you spend more time working on the actual problem rather than implementing 
helper methods.  
Hence, it’s a win-win both ways. 
 
2. For computer engineering fundamentals like OS, DBMS, CN, you can refer any YouTube 
playlist you feel comfortable. And if you had learnt these subjects well when (if) they 
were in your syllabus, you are good to go. Just do a quite revision a day before. 
 
3. Frame the answers to a few basic questions like "tell me about yourself", "what are your 
strengths", "what are your weaknesses", "where do you see yourself in a few years", etc. 
Be confident while answering these. Try to use the STAR method to answer situation-
based questions. Don’t worry if you can’t frame it this way. Even I didn’t follow any such 
convention, but it helps if you do. 
 
4. Read interview experiences from everywhere you can find: GFG, Glassdoor, this drive, 
etc. because sometimes you might be lucky to get the same question as the one in the 
experience and since you know how to respond / answer, you would feel more 
confident. 
 
5. Get well versed with your resume. You should know everything about the projects you 
put there. Even if it was a team project and your teammates have worked on parts of it, 
you should be able to give a brief explanation about that. And if it was you who worked 
on it, you should be able to explain the flow and give the reasoning for your choices. 
 
6. You can reach out to me here.
5 
 
ALL THE BEST! 
Even if you don’t get selected, stay persistent. All the happens, happens for a reason.
